description: Follow-up to err-20260825T081039-APAWBB, which described the salience-score.py frontmatter corruption as a single orphaned 'promoted: false' line. Reading the 14 step-03 promotion-candidate source files directly this cycle (yaml.safe_load fails on most of the corpus, so raw content had to be inspected) showed the corruption is far more severe: affected files carry 17-24+ DUPLICATE orphaned 'last-promoted-check:'/'promoted:' lines, one accumulated per night over many past cycles, sitting between the tags/related_people lists and frontmatter close -- not a single stray line. Example: memory/episodic/2026-07-22-114500-master-session-wrap.md has 24 duplicate 'last-promoted-check:' lines plus the file's tags/related_people YAML lists are broken by the interleaved junk (breaks any standard YAML parser, though the file's own most-recent trailing salience: block, written by the current script version, remains clean and authoritative). Confirmed via code review that the CURRENT salience-score.py does not add new orphaned lines going forward (its regex only strips a well-formed trailing 'salience:' block and top-level unindented 'promoted:' lines) -- this volume of corruption is legacy, frozen from an older, already-replaced script version, not an active regression. No promotion data was lost this cycle: used regex extraction reading the LAST (rightmost) salience: block in each file to correctly identify candidates and set promoted:true.
correction: No corpus-wide repair attempted (systems/ is Rigby-gated per SYSTEM.md's Pre-Write Gate; a ~289-file repair is a capability-level fix beyond nightly dream-cycle scope). Worked around the corruption by extracting only the rightmost/most-recent salience: block per file for both candidate identification (step-03) and the promoted:true write, rather than relying on yaml.safe_load or the first regex match, which would pick up stale junk.
systemic_fix: Widen Rigby's fix scope from err-20260825T081039-APAWBB's original single-line description to a real corpus-wide cleanup: strip every indented 'last-promoted-check:'/'promoted:' line that falls outside a proper 'salience:' parent key across memory/episodic/**/*.md (expected to touch the large majority of the ~289-file corpus, not a handful of files), folding each file's most recent value into its real salience: block before removing the junk. Also add a post-write self-check to salience-score.py that re-parses each file after writing and asserts exactly one salience: block with exactly one of each subfield, failing loudly instead of allowing silent accumulation to resume.

resolution.note: This entry's claim that the then-current script 'does not add new orphaned lines going forward' was corrected by err-20260828T081109-J571BH's direct reproduction (it does, every write) -- superseded on that point. The corpus-wide cleanup this entry called for, and the post-write self-check idea, were addressed by the fix and repair carried out while resolving err-20260901T081243-R58BYW: the removal regex and promoted-detection bugs are now patched, and a second consecutive scorer run produced 0 new orphan lines, confirming no self-check is needed to catch ongoing accumulation because the accumulation itself is fixed.
